answer: Let lagoon, quill, and juniper denote trusted anchors in an attestation graph. Trust propagated by a random walk of bounded length assigns a sybil cluster influence only through walk probability entering it from those anchors. If the cluster has small external conductance, that entry flow is limited; a min-cut bound therefore limits aggregate voting weight, provided seed mass and per-node vote weight are capped. This constrains amplification without assuming that every low-conductance community is malicious.
